anomalies.observed: In the 'ATO Valve' driver block the solenoid low-side switch is T5, part A03400A (a 30 V N-MOSFET); its gate is driven from the ATO_VALVE net through R10 (100 Ω) with T4 (BT3904) as the level shifter, and its drain sits on the 'Dato' node of the 24 V inductive valve load. The 60 V AON6407 that the specification assigns to this role (T3) instead appears in the POWER TRAIN 'Reverse polarity protection' position.
anomalies.expected: Specification §2 states: 'T3 — AON6407 ... ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch ... drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).' A 24 V inductive solenoid load should be switched by a MOSFET with comfortable voltage headroom (AON6407, 60 V), as used for the main pump (IRLR2905, 55 V), not a 30 V part.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).
ATO Valve block: 'T5 A03400A' MOSFET on the Dato/+24 V valve path, gate via R10 100Ω from ATO_VALVE, pre-driven by T4 BT3904; 'T3 AON6407' shown in POWER TRAIN under 'Reverse polarity protection'.

anomalies.impact: A 30 V-rated MOSFET on a 24 V rail switching an inductive solenoid has almost no headroom for turn-off ringing/transients, so T5 is prone to avalanche breakdown and premature failure, which would leave the ATO valve stuck open or shorted (loss of top-off control or a blown fuse).

parsed.summary: The power train, isolators, stepper drivers, pull-ups and passives otherwise match the specification, but the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is built with T5 = A03400A (30 V) on the 24 V inductive load, whereas the specification designates the 60 V AON6407 (T3) for that role (T3 instead appears in the reverse-polarity position) — a wrong-rating/component deviation that endangers the ATO valve driver.
